summary.en: Slide a pattern across every legal start, count overlapping matches, and measure the worst-case comparisons.
summary.bn: প্রতিটি শুরুর পজিশনে প্যাটার্ন মিলিয়ে দেখো, ওভারল্যাপ করা ম্যাচও গুনো, আর তুলনার খরচ হিসাব করো।

notes: The demonstrated programs use C17; the lesson states their input and arithmetic bounds.

examples.title: Count every overlapping occurrence
examples.explanationHtml: Input ababa aba reports starts zero and two, count two, comparisons seven. Try aaaaa aaa to see three overlapping matches. Every legal start is tested even after success.

examples.title: Stop at the first occurrence
examples.explanationHtml: The strncmp-based program returns the first matching position or minus one. It still tests complete pattern-sized windows, so the library comparison never reads beyond the validated string window.

examples.title: Choose a nonoverlapping policy
examples.explanationHtml: For aaaaa with pattern aa, the third program counts two nonoverlapping matches. After success it advances by two, while a mismatch advances by one. The ordinary overlapping count would be four.

practice.title: List all starts for text aaaaa and pattern aaa, including overlaps.
practice.statementHtml: List all starts for text aaaaa and pattern aaa, including overlaps.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: Legal starts are 0, 1 and 2. Each length-three window equals aaa. The total is three; moving by the pattern length would skip the overlapping matches.

practice.title: Count comparisons for text aaaaa and pattern aab.
practice.statementHtml: Count comparisons for text aaaaa and pattern aab.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: There are three legal starts. Each compares a with a, then a with a, then a with b. Three comparisons per start give nine. No start succeeds.

quiz.prompt: For text length five and pattern length three, how many alignments are legal?
quiz.explanation: Starts zero through two give n-m+1 alignments.

quiz.prompt: Why is start+m<=n used instead of start+m<n?
options: To include the final legal window
quiz.explanation: The final window ends exactly at n, the excluded text boundary.

quiz.prompt: How many overlapping matches does aaa have in aaaaa?
quiz.explanation: The valid starts are zero, one and two.

quiz.prompt: What should happen when the pattern is longer than the text?
Which input family causes long repeated failures?
options: Many a letters against a pattern ending in b
An empty text with a long pattern
quiz.explanation: Most characters match before the final mismatch, repeated at each start.

quiz.prompt: What is the worst-case time when 1<=m<=n?
quiz.explanation: Each of n-m+1 alignments can compare all m characters.

quiz.prompt: Which string model do the C demonstrations use?
quiz.explanation: The validated tokens contain one lowercase Latin byte per character and terminate with a zero byte.

quiz.prompt: How many legal windows of length three fit in a five-byte text?
quiz.explanation: Starts zero, one and two fit completely.

quiz.prompt: At alignment two, which text byte is compared with pattern position one in ababa?
quiz.explanation: The combined index is three, holding b.

quiz.prompt: What overlapping count does this two-letter comparison produce in aaaa?
quiz.explanation: All three adjacent pairs match, including the overlapping middle pair.

keyPoints.en: Test starts from zero through n minus m.
keyPoints.bn: শুরুর ইনডেক্স শূন্য থেকে n-m পর্যন্ত দেখো।

keyPoints.en: Restart pattern comparison at each alignment.
keyPoints.bn: প্রতিটি নতুন পজিশনে প্যাটার্নের শুরু থেকে তুলনা করো।

keyPoints.en: Moving one position after a match preserves overlaps.
keyPoints.bn: ম্যাচের পর এক ঘর সরলে ওভারল্যাপ করা ম্যাচও পাও।

keyPoints.en: A longer pattern has no legal alignment.
keyPoints.bn: প্যাটার্ন টেক্সটের চেয়ে বড় হলে মেলানোর জায়গা থাকে না।

keyPoints.en: Naive matching may inspect the whole pattern at every start.
keyPoints.bn: সরাসরি ম্যাচিংয়ে প্রতিটি শুরুতে পুরো প্যাটার্ন দেখতে হতে পারে।

examQuestions.question: State the invariant and justify the time and space costs of Naive String Matching.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Before each outer iteration, every earlier start has been classified. The inner loop maintains that the first j pattern bytes equal the aligned text bytes. A mismatch proves this alignment cannot match; reaching j==m proves every pattern byte agrees.

The outer loop visits every fitting start exactly once. It therefore reports every occurrence and no invalid one. Overlaps need no special exception because starts advance by one regardless of the previous result.

For 1<=m<=n, there are n-m+1 starts, each requiring at most m comparisons. The worst-case time is O((n-m+1)*m), commonly written O(nm). A text of many a letters and a pattern of many a letters ending in b forces long failures repeatedly.

If every first comparison fails, the scan uses one comparison per start. Input reading still costs O(n+m). Searching needs O(1) extra working space beyond the strings and any retained list of matches.

When m>n, there are no search alignments. We use signed lengths in the bounded demonstrations, avoiding unsigned subtraction n-m that could wrap to a huge value.
